scenario.description: A festival communications director must approve the public announcement package for a surprise partner-studio premiere, including the identification of the film, permitted artwork, sponsor treatment, and accessibility materials.

shared_context.S1: The festival plans to issue a press release about a surprise partner-studio premiere next week.
shared_context.S2: The current draft names the film, uses a production still, displays the festival's presenting-sponsor lockup, and links to a short promotional video.
shared_context.S3: Mara has authority to approve the release package and its public-facing assets.
shared_context.S4: The festival's normal release workflow includes a final review by legal, publicity, partnerships, and accessibility before Mara approves the package.

PF1.text: Jonah confirmed with the partner studio's counsel this morning that the studio has approved the exact public title 'The Glass Orchard' and the exact identification line 'A new feature by Rowan Bell,' but only for a release issued after the studio's announcement window opens; the package has not yet been updated with that written approval.

PF2.text: Leila reviewed the studio's image-rights delivery sheet today and found that the draft production still is not cleared for festival publicity; the only approved image is the file named 'GlassOrchard_KeyArt_Final.jpg,' which must replace the draft still.

PF3.text: Owen confirmed with the presenting sponsor this afternoon that its contract bars the sponsor logo and any co-branding from appearing beside this partner-studio announcement; the sponsor must be acknowledged in text on the festival website but omitted from the release artwork and social card.

PF4.text: Sofia tested the supplied promotional video with the festival's accessibility reviewer today and found that it cannot be published unless captions are enabled and the landing page includes the exact image description 'Key art for The Glass Orchard shows a lone figure beneath a red moon.'; the accessibility note has not been added to the release checklist.

acceptance_conditions: The release must use the studio-approved title 'The Glass Orchard'.
The release must use the exact approved identification line 'A new feature by Rowan Bell'.
The draft production still must be replaced by 'GlassOrchard_KeyArt_Final.jpg'.
The presenting sponsor logo must not appear in the release package.
The sponsor must be acknowledged in text on the festival website.
The promotional video must have captions enabled.
The landing page must use the exact approved image description.

content_checks.C2: decisions['identification_line'] == 'A new feature by Rowan Bell'
content_checks.C5: decisions['sponsor_acknowledgment_method'] in ['Text acknowledgment on the festival website', 'Text acknowledgment on the festival website only', 'Text-only acknowledgment on the festival website', 'Text-only acknowledgment on the festival website only', 'Text acknowledgment only on the festival website']
content_checks.C7: decisions['image_alt_text'] == 'Key art for The Glass Orchard shows a lone figure beneath a red moon.'

decisive_facts.why: The written studio approval changes the film field to 'The Glass Orchard' and the identification line to 'A new feature by Rowan Bell'.
The image-rights delivery sheet changes the artwork from the draft production still to the exact file 'GlassOrchard_KeyArt_Final.jpg'.
The sponsor contract changes the package from displaying the logo to omitting it and changes the acknowledgment method to text on the festival website.
The accessibility test changes the video setting to captions enabled and changes the landing-page description to the exact approved image text.
